Subject: How are shared conversation prefixes billed when multiple users reuse the same silo?

Hi Sergio,

Quick question from billing — we have a feature where customer service agents join the same conversation silo (shared context) and often trigger the same system prompt + product catalog prefix. Agents are different users but the conversation state (the "silo") is shared.

Two specific asks:
- If the system prompt + catalog prefix was loaded by Agent A and then Agent B sends a follow-up within 7m, does Redwood bill full tokens for the repeated prefix or is there any cross-session prefix crediting?
- How does minimum per-request rounding interact with short repeated calls? Our agents often send micro-updates that are 6-15 tokens of user input.

Sample: in a 24h window we see 4,200 requests to that silo. Average preserved prefix length 1,200 tokens; average user message 12 tokens. Our reconciliation shows a much larger token charge than expected (we assumed prefix reuse would reduce it).

Can you outline how Redwood would meter this and whether we can propose any adjustment or pilot? We can share a CSV with request-level events if helpful.

Elena — thanks for the clear write-up and the CSV. We're glad you sent concrete numbers; that helps.

Short answer up front: by default we bill for the tokens processed by the serving runtime per request; the runtime can reuse KV cache within a single process for the same conversation ID, but cross-user, cross-session reuse depends on how the silo is surfaced in the request (shared conversation_id vs separate session tokens) and on the TTL/affinity policy. There are a few levers we can use to reduce charges: prefix-cache affinity, short TTL window crediting, and a per-prefix amortization rule for identical prefixes within an account.

I'm looping in Karthik for the exact metering math and Marissa to discuss a commercial/credits pilot. Camila — FYI on potential docs/update to the pricing FAQ.

2) Pricing team (Marissa) to propose a pilot crediting structure (sample invoice lines so BrightCart can assess).
3) We'll send a short proposal with sample invoice rows and a timeline for a pilot.

Folks — dug into the CSV and our runtime traces. TL;DR: current metering behaves like this by default and I propose a conservative pilot option.

Current behavior (short form):
- If the request arrives with the same conversation_id and hits a warmed KV cache on the same GPU worker, the runtime does not re-stream the full prefix; server-side reuse reduces compute but we still surface the full model context length in logs for debugging. However, our billing RPC aggregates per-request token deltas and currently counts the prompt payload sent to the model invocation (we treat that as billable).
- If the client re-sends the prefix as part of the payload (rehydrated client-side), we bill full tokens that appear in the payload.
- There is a 10-token minimum rounding currently applied at invoice line item level for small streaming requests (legacy floor applied to microcalls). That explains why your 12-token messages look costlier.

Concrete numbers from your sample (approx):
- 4,200 requests, avg prefix 1,200 tokens, avg user 12 tokens
- If every request sent the full 1,200 token prefix -> naive billed tokens = 4,200*(1,200+12) = 5,054,400 tokens
- If runtime reuses prefix and only bills user tokens per request (best case) -> billed tokens = 4,200*12 = 50,400 tokens (but minimum floor 10 tokens will round smalls up; negligible here)

Pilot proposal (to reduce BrightCart's billed tokens while we iterate on infra):
Option A — Account-level prefix amortization (recommended conservative):
- For identical prefixes observed within an account and re-used within a rolling 15-minute window, bill the first request full prompt tokens, then bill only 20% of the prompt tokens on subsequent reuses within that window (keeps incentives aligned and shares benefit).
- Rounding: keep existing per-request 10-token floor but apply per-prefix amortization before flooring.
- Example invoice lines (sample day):
  1) Line: "Prompt (initial) — 1,200 tokens" qty 1 -> 1,200 tokens billed
  2) Line: "Prompt (amortized reuse, 4,199 occurrences) — 240 tokens each" qty 4,199 -> 1,007,760 tokens billed
  3) Line: "User messages (4,200 at 12 tokens)" -> 50,400 tokens billed
  Total billed tokens = 1,059,360 tokens (versus naive 5,054,400) — ~79% reduction.

Option B — Worker-level cache crediting (higher infra requirement):
- If request hits the same warmed worker within 5 minutes, mark prompt as "worker-cached" and bill 5% of prompt tokens for that hit. This reduces charges more but requires routing guarantees and tracing.

Operational notes and risks:
- We need robust deduplication logic to compare prefix fingerprints (hash prefix payload) — small variants (timestamped tokens) will be treated as different prefixes unless normalized.
- Auditability: every amortized line will include a "reuse_count" column in billing exports so customers can reconcile (we'll add to billing CSVs).

Attachments: I attached a compact sample invoice PDF and the annotated CSV (prefix_usage_example.csv) showing which requests would be amortized.

If BrightCart likes Option A we can stand up a billing pilot for a fixed window (30 days) and generate a credit to make you whole for a one-week lookback. Marissa — can you propose commercial terms (discount rate vs credit size)?

Karthik
Principal, Serving Runtime

Elena — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and a concrete pilot offer below.

Summary of how we charge today:
- Full prompt tokens are billable when the payload sent to the model contains them. If the client supplies the prefix in the request body we bill those tokens. If the runtime satisfies the request from an internal KV cache without re-sending the prompt to the model, charges are lower in practice but not currently amortized on invoice lines.

Our recommended pilot (Option A — account-level prefix amortization):
- Rolling 15-minute prefix window keyed by prefix fingerprint and account ID.
- First seen: bill full prompt tokens. Reuse within 15m: bill 20% of prompt tokens for each reuse.
- Keep 10-token per-request floor but apply amortization before flooring.
- Pilot length: 30 days; retrospective credit for the first 7 days while we validate reconciliation (we will provide a granular CSV for your finance team).
- Expected impact based on your sample: ~79% reduction vs naive "prefix always billed" model; we estimate billed tokens down to ~1.06M for the same activity.

Attachments: sample invoice rows attached (proposed-invoice-lines.pdf) and the annotated CSV you provided.

Ask: please confirm you are comfortable with Option A pilot and whether your finance team needs a PO or contractual amendment. We can run the pilot under the existing usage metric (no contract amendment) and provide credits for the agreed retrospective window, or we can formalize in a short SOW if you'd like a committed pilot.

Next steps after you confirm:
- Marissa will send proposed credit/discount terms and the SOW language (if needed).
- Karthik & infra will enable amortization flags for your account and add a "reuse_count" column in the billing export.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute sync to walk the finance team through the sample invoice.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.
